newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB chief says April wheat exports threatened.
newsitem.headline: CWB chief says April wheat exports threatened.

text.p: Canadian spring wheat exports in April may be hurt by a rail shipping delay that has kept more than 1.5 million tonnes of grain from reaching Pacific ports since January, Canadian Wheat Board chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said.
"We can't deliver into those (Japan and Pacific Rim) countries in February and March, and it's very tight for April as well until we get this backlog cleared up," Hehn told Reuters.
There were 42 vessels waiting to load on Canada's Pacific Coast on Monday with 13 more ships due by week's end, he said.
"The situation is deteriorating. There's 13 ships due this week, if they all show up we'll be further behind," he said.
Shippers have blamed the delays on heavy snow, cold and sporadic Prairie elevator grain deliveries.
Hehn asked Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale last week to persuade railways to expedite shipment now that the wheat board faces more than C$15 million in demurrage penalties.

Rail rates on grain cannot exceed a federally mandated cap, and transportation industry analysts said other commodities may be getting priority over grain. The Canadian government is due to review the grain rail rate cap in 1999.
Canadian National Railway Co spokesman Jim Feeny said his firm's delivery performance on grain to Pacific ports continued to improve this week but declined to provide details.
Officials at Canadian Pacific unit CP Rail System were not immediately available for comment.
